original.description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. original.description: Objective: To develop a low SwaP breadboard of a full laser system that will manipulate Rydberg atom in vapour cell, and be able tobe configured for sensing applications for RF receivers.Description: Highly-excited atoms, often known as Rydberg atoms, display extreme sensitivity to external electromagnetic (EM) fields, including the electric fields associated with black-body radiation (BBR).In addition to their use in quantum computing, Rydberg atoms can be configured for sensing applications. Such sensors make use of non-destructive read-out of Rydberg states, which is implemented optically, including fluorescence detection of low-lying Rydberg states. A range of different Rydberg sensing modalities have been developed; these include those developed for microwave standards andimaging in the Terahertz regime to sensitive digital communications techniques in radio and microwave bands. This activity developsa complete laser system needed to perform an RF instrument based on Alkali Rydberg Atomic Sensors. To do so the selection of the relevant parameters to address the sensor is aimed to be done by consolidating the first set of requirements. A dedicated focus is to be addressed towards a low SWaP (Size, Weight and Power) for CubeSAT platform. This shall ensure a proper design and manufacturing of the Laser system. This breadboard is then tested on an adequate Rydberg sensor for RF measurement. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement review for laser system to manipulate Rydberg atom - Design of a compact laser system - Manufacturing of the laser system - Test on Rydberg Atom and validation of the RF instrument.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. The performance of such system will be evaluated with the development of a system simulator.Targeted Improvements: - Reduce by 80% the cost of the satellite system for FRMCS.- Reduce by 50% the cost of on-board railway terminals, by allowing a single terminal solution for terrestrial and satellite FRMCS connectivity.Description: The Future RailwayMobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. Through standardisation work, satcom is established as a component of the future system, while it is found that the satellite integration into FRMCS is simplified when satcom is employing the 5G NR, which is the selected air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. However, the frequency bands for such a service via satellite and the design of the satellite system are yetto be concluded. The advantages of an innovative approach, where the satellite offers connectivity exclusively to the coverage gapsofsuch terrestrial network, have been recently reported. In fact, such a satellite system targeting only the terrestrial coverage gaps while ignoring the areas serviced by theterrestrial network, will have a lower complexity and overall cost, as fewer satellites of less capacity will be required. In addition, such a satellite system will be able to operate in the same frequency bands as theterrestrial network (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), as each network (terrestrial or satellite) will not be available in the same area where the other network operates and therefore they will not interfere with each other. This usage of the same frequency from the satellite and the terrestrial network not only facilitates the integration of the two networks into FRMCS, but also potentially allow the usage of the same terminal for both networks, a solution that is very favourable for railway operators. This activity will thereforeinvestigate the design of a 5G NR based satellite system for FRMCS which exclusively targets the terrestrial network gaps of communication and operates in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial FRMCS network. The activity will include a traffic characterisation and capacity analysis for the terrestrial network gaps which will then feed the system design and the element sizing of the ground and space components. The impact of the railway-satellite channel for the 900 MHz and the 1900 GHz will also be thoroughly investigated. The best numerologies and 5G NR configurations will also be identified for such a satellite system. The work will be supported by the development of a system simulator which will investigate the FRMCS 5G NR satellite link performance and achieved C/I ratios under a variety of different orbits, system architectures, frequency bands, channel conditions and air interface configurations. The activity will also investigate and conclude on the feasibility of having a single modem and a single antenna equipped on board the trains, which offer connectivity both to the satellite and the terrestrial network at different time instances.

original.description: As part of the Greek National Satellite Space Project - Phase 2, the objective of this activity is the procurement of Phase A/B1 for an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) mission aimed at the development and in-space demonstration of a flexible small-satellite platformenabling future In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing (ISAM) missions.The mission shall demonstrate autonomous rendezvous,inspection and close-proximity operations (CPO) capabilities in orbit, while supporting the development of European industrial andcommercial capabilities and fostering future operational services.The mission shall address identified user needs and market opportunities with the objective of contributing to the development of future European in-space infrastructure and services. Tenderers shall therefore propose a mission concept that combines technology demonstration objectives with a credible path towards future operational applications.The mission and system development approach shall be based on a modular and scalable architecture, supported byanincremental demonstration strategy with clearly defined primary and extended objectives.
